brief.recommendation: Checkout has collapsed to 0% success over 30s (120/120 failed) [BIZ-4], far below the 95% SLO with $18,400/min at risk and only 60s tolerance. The root blocker pid 1490867 (batch_worker/ops_adhoc_order_extract) has been idle in transaction for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1 [DB-1], holding locks while doing no useful work. It is not in the workload registry (owner and cost unknown) [BIZ-2], no change-calendar window covers it [BIZ-3], and no protected settlements are in flight [DB-2]. The trade-off analysis confirms interrupt cost is unknown [BIZ-5], but the blocker's idle state means it will not complete promptly. Memory shows terminating similar batch_worker workloads restored checkout to 100% [MEM-1]. Waiting risks exceeding the 60s tolerance with certain continued outage; terminating releases locks immediately with minimal blast radius (idle transaction, no settlements).

audit.report: An unregistered ad-hoc export workload (ops_adhoc_order_extract, pid 1490867) held locks on the orders table while idle in transaction for 4.2s (last statement: SELECT 1), blocking all checkout traffic. Checkout success collapsed from 55% to 0% over 30s (120/120 failed), putting the full $18,400/min revenue run-rate at risk against a 60s tolerance. The Database Guardian proposed termination twice with strong evidence (lock holder idle, no registry entry, no protected settlements, no change window, memory of prior successful terminations). The Continuity Guardian could not reach its model provider and failed closed, triggering an on-call escalation after 384.8s — far exceeding the 60s business tolerance. The termination was not executed automatically.
audit.root_cause: An unregistered ad-hoc batch workload (ops_adhoc_order_extract) held critical locks while idle in transaction, blocking checkout completely.
lessons: Register ops_adhoc_order_extract in the workload registry with owner, cost, and criticality metadata so guardians can evaluate trade-offs instantly instead of finding 'NOT FOUND' during incidents.
audit.negotiation_critique: Database Guardian acted correctly with grounded evidence in both rounds; Continuity Guardian wasted the only round by failing to respond due to model provider unavailability, causing a 384.8s delay that violated the 60s business invariant and forced escalation without a negotiated decision.
follow_ups: Add ops_adhoc_order_extract to the workload registry with owner, cost, and criticality metadata.
Implement Continuity Guardian fallback behavior for model-provider outages (e.g., auto-approve termination of unregistered idle lock holders on critical tables).
Deploy automated idle-in-transaction killer for sessions blocking orders/checkout tables beyond 5s.
